tool_input.command:
cd ~/source/personal/blog-posts/url-shortener-loop-sample
rm -rf /tmp/t4test && mkdir -p /tmp/t4test
DATABASE_PATH=/tmp/t4test/t4.db npm run --silent migrate
DATABASE_PATH=/tmp/t4test/t4.db PORT=3204 node dist/main.js &
SERVER_PID=$!
sleep 1.5
echo "--- health ---"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3204/health
echo "--- create ---"
CREATE=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3204/links -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"url":"https://example.com/a/very/long/path"}')
echo "$CREATE"
SLUG=$(echo "$CREATE" | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(d).slug))")
echo "slug=$SLUG"
echo "--- redirect 1 ---"
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - http://127.0.0.1:3204/$SLUG | grep -i -E "HTTP|location"
echo "--- redirect 2 ---"
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - http://127.0.0.1:3204/$SLUG | grep -i -E "HTTP|location"
echo "--- read link ---"
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3204/links/$SLUG
echo
echo "--- health again (must not be shadowed) ---"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3204/health
kill -TERM $SERVER_PID
wait $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"

result: T4 is done: I implemented `GET /:slug` (redirect + hit increment via a new `RedirectController`) and `GET /links/:slug` (pure read) on the existing `LinksController`, with `findBySlug`/`incrementHits` added to the repository. T4's own gate passes, and I re-verified T1–T3's gates plus `npm test` to confirm no regressions. Reported `outcome: done` in `loop/proposal.json` for the driver to pick up.
